findings.classification: Confirmed for Debian; strongly supported for Windows
findings.title: The current untagged checkout generates invalid native package versions
findings.evidence: The repository has zero remote tags (git ls-remote --tags origin). At the reviewed HEAD git describe --always returns f3a248b. The Debian build removes only an optional leading v, then writes f3a248b into DEBIAN/control Version. A local minimal control fixture with that exact value fails dpkg-deb --build with exit 2: 'Version field value f3a248b: version number does not start with digit'. The Windows path computes VERSION_NUM=f3a248b.0 and passes it to Inno Setup VersionInfoVersion, which accepts only a numeric quad (also acknowledged by the script comments).
findings.impact: Current default-branch Debian builds cannot produce an installable package; Windows installer compilation also receives an invalid version. CI explicitly runs these paths for master pushes/PRs.
findings.recommendation: Separate semantic/numeric package version from the git display identifier. Supply a validated release version and valid untagged development fallback, such as Debian 0.0.0+git.<sha> and Windows 0.0.0.0; retain the SHA in display/build metadata. Add cheap package-version checks before compiling.
findings.validation: Confirmed with git describe, remote tag enumeration, and an actual dpkg-deb fixture build (exit 2). Full native builds were not run; Windows Inno compilation was not available. Regression validation should cover an untagged checkout, an annotated release tag, a lightweight release tag, and commits after a release tag.

findings.classification: Strongly supported by actual watchdog execution and Flatpak's documented deletion semantics
findings.title: Ordinary Flatpak removal leaves the privileged host manager installed indefinitely
findings.evidence: The watchdog equates the existence of ~/.var/app/io.geph.GephGui with continued installation and exits at line 17. Flatpak retains application data during ordinary uninstall; deleting it is the separate --delete-data option. The current upstream command documentation states this option removes app data in ~/.var/app (flatpak/flatpak doc/flatpak-uninstall.xml, file blob cc29c049667b6369ba2a8a429facbdd2ed0fec62). An actual safe invocation of the unchanged watchdog with an existing retained data directory and no installed binaries returns 0 immediately, without attempting unregister-manager.
findings.impact: After a normal flatpak uninstall, the privileged Geph manager/service, engine binaries and cleanup timer remain installed and potentially running. The advertised automatic uninstall cleanup never occurs unless the user separately deletes app data.
findings.recommendation: Determine actual app installation state across the relevant user/system Flatpak installations, retaining manager ownership for other users, or provide an explicit supported host-manager uninstall action. Do not use app-data presence as the install-state signal.
findings.validation: Executed the current watchdog safely against a temporary existing app-data directory, confirming immediate successful no-op. Consulted current Flatpak source documentation and option declaration. A full flatpak install/uninstall cycle and privileged service removal were not run. Regression validation should exercise both normal uninstall and --delete-data, with multiple-user ownership considered.

findings.title: The untagged checkout produces invalid native package versions
findings.evidence_classification: Confirmed Debian failure; Windows rejection strongly supported by the generated nonnumeric value and Inno's numeric VersionInfoVersion contract

source_locations.meaning: Use git describe --always, remove only v, and write that value into control Version.
Derive VERSION_NUM by stripping v and a suffix, then append .0.
Pass VERSION_NUM into the numeric-only VersionInfoVersion field.
Default-branch CI invokes these build paths without supplying a separate semantic version.

findings.observed_failure: This repository has zero remote tags. At the pinned HEAD, git describe --always returns f3a248b. Debian receives Version=f3a248b and dpkg-deb exits 2 because it does not start with a digit. Windows receives VERSION_NUM=f3a248b.0, which is not a numeric quad.
findings.user_impact: Maintainers cannot build a Debian artifact from the current default branch using the documented build entry point; Windows installer compilation also receives invalid version metadata. This blocks ordinary branch builds before usable artifacts can be produced.

repair.preferred_change: Define validated native package versions independently of the git display identifier. Require an explicit release semantic version or a recognized release tag; for an untagged development checkout generate a valid fallback such as Debian 0.0.0+git.<sha> and Windows 0.0.0.0. Preserve git describe output in artifact/display build metadata. Validate versions before expensive compilation.

findings.title: Ordinary Flatpak removal does not trigger privileged host-manager cleanup
findings.evidence_classification: Strongly supported by source, actual watchdog execution, and current upstream Flatpak deletion semantics

source_locations.meaning: Exit while the app-data directory exists, regardless of actual installed application state.
Install /usr/local/bin manager/engine, register its service, and enable the cleanup timer.
Pass the data directory as the watchdog's sole ownership signal.

findings.observed_failure: Normal Flatpak uninstall retains ~/.var/app data; --delete-data is a separate option. The unchanged watchdog returns successful no-op when that retained directory exists, even with no installed binaries in the supplied temporary bindir.
findings.user_impact: A user who removes the Flatpak can retain an installed and potentially running privileged host manager, engine, and cleanup timer indefinitely. Deleting app data while the Flatpak remains installed is also not reliable proof that the host manager should be removed.

repair.preferred_change: Replace the data-directory heuristic with explicit packaging ownership and verified installation state. Record the owning user/installation context in a root-owned record during privileged installation, reconcile all supported owners, and unregister only the matching packaging-owned host manager after no owner remains. If reliable cross-installation reconciliation cannot be implemented and tested immediately, replace the automatic promise with an explicit supported host-manager uninstall action; do not retain destructive automation keyed only to app-data deletion.
repair.open_design_decision: Choose and document ownership when user/system Flatpaks, multiple users, or a Debian-managed host service coexist. The existing global service and /usr/local/bin paths do not encode this ownership. This handoff does not authorize a new service architecture.
change_surface: flatpak/install-host-manager.sh: persist validated installation/owner context and manager identity
flatpak/geph-flatpak-watchdog.sh: query installation state and reconcile owners before removal
flatpak/geph-cleanup.service and geph-cleanup.timer: pass a root-owned ownership record instead of raw app-data existence
Flatpak bootstrap contract in pinned gephgui-wry dependency: inspect and coordinate argument changes; dependency source was not reviewed here
User-facing Flatpak installation/removal documentation or explicit uninstall entry point
invariants: Retaining app data after uninstall does not prevent removal of an otherwise unowned host manager.
Deleting app data alone does not remove a manager still needed by an installed application.
One user removing a Flatpak does not remove a manager still needed by another supported owner.
A Flatpak cleanup operation never unregisters an unrelated Debian or manually installed manager.
Unknown installation state or unreadable ownership metadata retains the manager and reports a diagnostic rather than guessing.
Cleanup is idempotent and does not broaden deletion outside exact packaging-owned files/services.
Ownership records and executable paths consumed by a privileged cleanup action cannot be replaced by an unprivileged user.
acceptance_criteria: Normal uninstall with retained data eventually cleans an unowned packaging manager, or the documented explicit uninstall action demonstrably does so.
Uninstall with --delete-data produces the same host cleanup result.
Data reset while the app remains installed does not tear down the manager.
Multiple-user and user/system installation cases follow the documented ownership policy.
An unrelated host-manager service survives the cleanup test.
Interrupted or repeated cleanup converges without deleting foreign policy, data, or executables.
regression_cases: Installed app whose data was manually removed
Manager binary/service belongs to another packaging method
risks: Incorrect owner reconciliation can remove a live privileged networking manager and disrupt connectivity.
Running per-user Flatpak queries from a root cleanup context requires deliberate user/installation selection.
The existing argument-templating/bootstrap contract lives partly in a separate gitlink dependency and must be traced before changing installer arguments.
repair.rollback: Restore prior installer assets only with automatic destructive cleanup disabled until ownership is verified. Keep the explicit manager removal route available. Preserve root-owned ownership records and service identity evidence across rollback; do not delete retained user app data as a cleanup workaround.
